note: AUDIT WARN EXPLAINED (row-count anomaly, median 2497.5: PFC1, PFC2). Not item-code conflation. For PFC1-PFC5 the absent response category is the top option 'Very easy': those five items run n=1069-2145 against a median of 2535 for the other 51 items in the batch, and the deficit tracks item easiness (Spearman about -0.8; PFC1 'open a previously opened jar' has both the largest deficit, n=1069, and the highest mean resp, 4.48). That is what dropping the easiest response produces, and it is not what a category collapse would produce. A property of the response data, not an itemtext defect.

AUDIT WARN EXPLAINED (row-count anomaly, median 12991: misperception1_1 .. misperception3_2). The administered form randomises the misperception blocks, showing each respondent one of three, so the six misperception codes each carry roughly a third of the sample while the rest of the table carries all of it. Applicability-driven missingness by design, not conflation. The mapping itself is an explicit numbering match, not an order inference: the registration workbooks number the statements B.1.1 to B.3.2 and the codes run misperception1_1 to misperception3_2.

AUDIT WARN EXPLAINED (row-count anomaly, median 12840: secondary_stressors__5, __8 .. __14). The secondary-stressor block is conditional, and the per-index counts follow the branch that gates them: indices 1-4 general at about n=10,000 each, 5 relationship at 6,607, 6-7 occupation at 9,905 and 9,623, 10-11 student at about 1,140, 12-13 children at about 3,200, 14 others at 8,359. The order shipped is the administered form's, which fits that conditional structure at 12 of the 14 positions; the workbooks' order is contradicted by the data and was not used.

AUDIT WARN EXPLAINED, two separate notes. (1) Row-count anomaly (median 3821.5: compliance_1 .. compliance_8): the eight compliance items were shown to everyone (n about 15,300 each) while the two social-influence norm blocks went to a subset (n about 3,800 each), so the compliance items sit far above the median. Design, not conflation. (2) '47.6% of rows have blank option_text': 80 of the 168 shipped option rows carry the canonical NA token. Those are the unlabelled midpoints of the two socialinfluence_nor* ladders, where the instrument labels only the endpoints ('Nearly nobody'/'Nearly everybody', 'Not important at all'/'Very important'); the compliance block's seven-point agree ladder is fully labelled. Genuinely unlabelled scale points, left blank rather than padded, which audit_batch.R notes rather than warns on.
